description: How Excel stores an error it has no literal for, which errorType names which error, and whether Excel reads the errors ts-xlsx writes. Excel computed and pasted errors over COM and saved the workbook (`an-error-value-is-stored-as-excel-stores-it/excel-saved.xlsx`). Each errorType 0 to 40 was then put, alone, in a constant cell of that package and read back. Packages ts-xlsx wrote were opened interactively and read back over COM, and a bisect against Excel's own package isolated why a formula's cached rich-value error shows as #VALUE! under manual calculation.
probe: a one-off COM script to author (Range.Formula2, PasteSpecial xlPasteValues); tools/excel-oracle/observe.ps1 to read Range.Text and Value2 back; .claude/skills/excel-gui-automation/scripts/open-verdict.ps1 for the open verdicts

authored.A1: Formula2 =SEQUENCE(3), with A2 holding a value

excelSaved.A1: <c r="A1" t="e" cm="1" vm="1"><f t="array" aca="1" ref="A1" ca="1">_xlfn.SEQUENCE(3)</f><v>#VALUE!</v></c>
excelSaved.G1: <c r="G1" t="e" vm="1"><v>#VALUE!</v></c>, sharing A1's rich value
excelSaved.G2: <c r="G2" t="e" vm="2"><v>#VALUE!</v></c>, sharing C1's rich value
excelSaved.xl/metadata.xml: metadataTypes XLDAPR then XLRICHVALUE; six XLRICHVALUE future-metadata blocks, each <xlrd:rvb i> in <ext uri="{3e2802c4-a4d2-4d8b-9148-e3be6c30e623}">; six valueMetadata blocks <rc t="2" v="n">
excelSaved.xl/richData/rdrichvaluestructure.xml: three _error structures: colOffset, errorType, rwOffset, subType (the spills); errorType, subType (the #CALC!s); errorType, field, subType (the #FIELD!)
excelSaved.xl/richData/rdrichvalue.xml: A1 errorType 8 subType 1 rwOffset 2; C1 errorType 13 subType 3; E1 errorType 12 field x; I1 errorType 13 subType 24; J1 errorType 8 subType 6; A1048576 errorType 8 subType 3
excelSaved.xl/richData/rdRichValueTypes.xml: global key flags for _Self, _DisplayString and eight other keys, none an error's
excelSaved.workbook: rdRichValue, rdRichValueStructure and rdRichValueTypes relationships under http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/2017/06/relationships, declared application/vnd.ms-excel.rdrichvalue+xml, rdrichvaluestructure+xml and rdrichvaluetypes+xml

errorTypeReadBack.note: One constant cell <c t="e" vm="1"><v>#VALUE!</v></c> naming a rich value of structure _error {errorType, subType 0}. cvErr is Value2 as an XlCVError number.

writtenByTsXlsx.the six errors as constants, as cached f: opened clean interactively; every constant read back as authored, Text and CVErr
writtenByTsXlsx.Excel's package read and written back: opened clean interactively; every error cell read back as in Excel's package
writtenByTsXlsx.the authored package without rdRichValue: opened clean interactively and read back the same, so the writer does not emit that part
writtenByTsXlsx.OOXML validator: the authored package, the rewrite and Excel's package all valid

manualCalculation.observed: With calcMode set to manual, Excel's own package showed every formula's cached rich-value error; the library's rewrite showed #VALUE!, flagged stale, on the formula cells and the right error on the pasted constants.
manualCalculation.bisect: Excel's package with the library's sheet, metadata and rich-value parts in place of its own still showed the errors; with the library's workbook part in place of its own it showed #VALUE!. Removing <fileVersion>, or the microsoft.com:RD feature from the xcalcf:calcFeatures extension, from Excel's own workbook part made the same four formula cells show #VALUE!. Adding calcId to the library's workbook part changed nothing.
manualCalculation.declared: A package ts-xlsx wrote, A1 a dynamic array caching #SPILL!, C1 a FILTER caching #CALC! and B1 =1+1 caching 5, with only its workbook part patched and read over COM. Under manual calculation A1 and C1 showed #SPILL! and #CALC! only with all three of <fileVersion appName="xl" lastEdited="7" lowestEdited="7" rupBuild="30326"/>, the microsoft.com:RD feature (alone or beside the six others Excel declares) and calcId="191029", the build's own engine. Without any one of them both showed #VALUE!, as they did with calcId="171027" or with a fileVersion of lastEdited and lowestEdited alone; a fileVersion of appName="xl" alone made the open fail. B1 showed 5 in every manual variant. Under automatic calculation every variant, declarations and calcId included, recalculated on open: A1 #SPILL!, B1 2, C1 #CALC!.

verdict: An error Excel has no literal for is <v>#VALUE!</v> with a vm resolving through XLRICHVALUE value metadata to a rich value of structure _error; its errorType names the error. 8 to 13 are #SPILL!, #CONNECT!, #BLOCKED!, #UNKNOWN!, #FIELD! and #CALC!, and 3, 4 and 6 read back as #REF!, #NAME? and #N/A; the numbers whose text and CVErr code disagree, or that fall back to #VALUE!, name nothing. The rich value's other keys and the types part are not needed for Excel to read the error. Under manual calculation, a formula's cached rich-value error shows only in a workbook part claiming Excel's own fileVersion, the RD calculation feature and the calcId of the engine opening it. The writer declares none of them: that claims a calculation by a named Excel build, holds only until the next engine, and under automatic calculation Excel recalculates the package on open whatever it declares. Locked by the corpus case an-error-value-is-stored-as-excel-stores-it.
